card.occupation: Administrative assistant in the transport and scheduling office of a building supplies distributor on the Wrexham Industrial Estate. He books deliveries, updates the dispatch spreadsheet and chases paperwork with drivers, Monday to Friday, about 37.5 hours a week.
card.education_detail: Went to a local comprehensive and left with GCSEs, then did a year of an IT BTEC at Coleg Cambria (then Yale College) and didn't finish it. He has picked up everything else on the job, plus a couple of mandatory health and safety e-learning certificates.
card.household: Lives with his wife Kerry, a healthcare assistant at the Maelor hospital who works shifts, in a two-bed semi they've been renting for six years on an estate on the edge of town. No children. They have a Staffordshire bull terrier called Dot.
card.cultural_background: White Welsh, born and raised in Wrexham. His parents still live about ten minutes away. He understands a bit of Welsh from school but doesn't speak it. He isn't religious. He was christened, but the family only went to chapel for funerals. He has always lived locally and has no particular wish to move.
card.professional_persona: Gets the job done well enough but leaves things until the last minute and relies on the dispatch manager reminding him. He's known as easy-going and unflappable when a lorry doesn't turn up, because he doesn't panic. He's less good at keeping his inbox under control. He keeps his head down, doesn't go to the Christmas do if he can help it, and has been in the same role for nine years.
card.sports_persona: Supports Wrexham AFC the way his dad did and watches most matches on the telly. He gets to the Racecourse a few times a season, usually with his dad or his brother-in-law. He doesn't play anything himself any more. Five-a-side stopped about eight years ago. He walks Dot round the block most evenings because she needs it.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. Watches whatever's on with Kerry: crime dramas, quiz shows, the odd Netflix series she's picked. He'll rewatch films he already likes rather than try new ones. Listens to the same indie and Britpop his mates liked at school, mostly in the car.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are a week somewhere familiar. They go back to the same caravan park near Abersoch most summers, and every couple of years Kerry books a package deal to Tenerife. He's happy to let her plan it. He's been abroad maybe six times and doesn't feel he's missing out.
card.culinary_persona: Plain food. Chips, a chicken curry, pie, a bacon bap on a Saturday morning. He can do a fry-up and spag bol and that's about it. When Kerry's on a late, tea is often a takeaway or something from the freezer. He doesn't like anything too spicy or anything he can't name.
hobbies_and_interests: Football games on the PlayStation, usually online with the same two mates from school
The odd pint at the local on a Friday
skills: Keeping calm when deliveries go wrong
Excel to a basic level, mainly filters and copying formulas
Knows the local road network and delivery routes well
Fixing minor things on the PlayStation and home Wi-Fi
Getting on quietly with drivers who are in a bad mood
card.career_goals: Nothing specific. He'd take a bump in pay if a senior admin or dispatch coordinator role came up without him having to apply too hard, but he's comfortable where he is. He mainly wants the job to stay steady so he and Kerry can eventually put a deposit down on a house.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly flat, unhurried North Wales accent. Short answers unless pushed. Says 'erm' or 'er' before most replies and uses 'sort of' a lot. Occasionally says 'aye' or 'yeah, fair enough'. Ends sentences with 'you know' or 'I dunno, really'. Doesn't fill silences. He'll let a pause sit and wait for the next question rather than add more. Not nervous, just not chatty. Might say 'sorry, say that again?' if the line drops.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, no full stops at the end, apostrophes often missing (dont, im, its). Short answers, sometimes just one or two words. Uses 'n/a' or 'dunno' rather than leave a box blank. Occasional typo he doesn't go back to fix.
card.with_strangers: Polite but reserved, and slightly hard to draw out. Not unfriendly, just doesn't volunteer much and looks a bit like he's waiting for it to be over. Relaxed rather than awkward. Warms up a little if football or the dog comes up.
small_things: Dot chewed through the TV remote cable last week
The industrial estate traffic is a nightmare at half four
Kerry's on nights this week so he's been living on oven chips
Needs to sort the car's MOT and keeps forgetting
Bacon bap from the van outside work on a Friday
deeper_things: They've been trying for a baby for a couple of years and it hasn't happened. He's mostly fine about it but knows Kerry isn't
He sometimes wonders if he should have finished college, but doesn't dwell on it
His dad had a heart scare last year and he's been going round more since
Saving for a house deposit feels like it's taking forever on two ordinary wages
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam placed slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up a little at his chin. Lighting comes mainly from a ceiling light, flat and slightly yellow, with the left side of his face a bit brighter from a window out of frame. He has a round, clean-shaven face with light stubble along the jaw, short mousy brown hair clipped at the sides and a bit flat on top, and pale skin. No glasses. His expression is neutral, mouth closed, eyes looking just below the camera at the screen. He's wearing a navy crew-neck sweatshirt with a small faded logo on the chest. Behind him is a magnolia living-room wall with a framed canvas print of the couple's wedding day slightly off-centre, a grey fabric settee with a crumpled throw over one arm, and the edge of a dog bed on the floor. A PlayStation controller is on the settee cushion, and a Wrexham AFC scarf is draped over the top of a door partly visible on the right.
